stem: A historian compares Buffalo Bill's show with Frederick Jackson Turner's 1893 essay. What is the most useful comparison?

stimulus.source_note: Buffalo Bill's Wild West poster, 1899 (Library of Congress, LCCN94513621). Public domain. Image viewed before writing.
stimulus.text: The poster advertises 'Buffalo Bill's Wild West and Congress of Rough Riders of the World,' 1899. At the right, Colonel W. F. Cody, 'Buffalo Bill,' sits on horseback, with the promise that he 'will appear at every performance.' The center shows 'Arab Horsemen' galloping and acrobats performing, and the banner at the bottom advertises 'the real Sons of the Soudan' and their feats of strength and horsemanship.

options.text: Both turned the closing West into a story about American character
Both argued that the West had never really existed
options.misconception: Background: Turner argued the frontier had shaped America; Cody staged the West as real and present, not as a fiction.

options.text: Both were written to defend the Dawes Act
options.misconception: Background: neither the show nor Turner's essay defends allotment; their subject is the meaning of the frontier.

options.text: Both ignored the West entirely and wrote about eastern cities
options.misconception: Background: the West is the whole subject of both, one on a poster and one in an essay.

rationales.A: Cody staged the West as daring and freedom. Background: Turner argued the frontier had made Americans democratic and self-reliant, and both made the West a story about what America is, and both left out the peoples the West had cost the most.
rationales.B: Background: Turner argued the frontier had shaped America. Cody staged the West as real and present, not as a fiction.
rationales.C: Background: neither the show nor Turner's essay defends allotment. Their subject is the meaning of the frontier.
rationales.D: Background: the West is the whole subject of both, one on a poster and one in an essay.
rationales.general:
Picture a showman and a scholar, both explaining the same West in the same decade.
1. Ask what Cody claims. His riders and sharpshooters show a West of daring and freedom.
2. Ask what Turner claims. Background: The frontier made Americans democratic and self-reliant.
3. Name what they share. Both turn the closing West into a story about American character.
Remember: a show and a thesis can tell the same story, one with horses and one with footnotes.
